msg_1_subject: Payment freeze proposal & VAT evidence request — Apex Insurance (INV-44911)
msg_1_body:
Hi Elena,

Following up on invoice INV-44911 (issued 2028-08-01) for $125,000 USD — our records show the invoice is 48 days overdue. We value the partnership with Apex Insurance; we also need to keep receivables within our credit parameters.

Requested actions: 
- Please confirm payment date for full settlement or a firm staggered payment plan within 7 business days (by 2028-09-25).
- Provide VAT documentation: if you are applying reverse-charge or zero-rate treatment, we need the VAT certificate / PO line showing tax exemption and remittance confirmation to validate the invoice.

If we do not receive payment confirmation or acceptable VAT evidence by end of day 2028-09-25, we will place the account on a temporary service freeze (API key throttle/credit hold) while collections and finance work through a payment pathway. This is a standard step for overdue balances of this size.

I attached the invoice (INV-44911.pdf) and our remittance instructions. If you prefer a staged payment, outline proposed dates and amounts and we will route for approval.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Manager, Accounts Receivable
Redwood Inference

Attachments: INV-44911.pdf (invoice), remittance_instructions.pdf
msg_2_subject: Re: Payment freeze proposal & VAT evidence request — Apex Insurance (INV-44911)
msg_2_body:
Hi Kimberly,

Apologies for the delay and thank you for the clear note. We are currently held up in our procurement approvals due to a vendor consolidation review. I have pushed the request through and expect the team to release funds, but it will take longer than your 7 business day window.

Proposed staged payment: 30% ($37,500) by 2028-09-29, remainder 70% by 2028-11-01. We can provide a remittance file for the first tranche by next week.

Regarding VAT: please find attached our PO (PO-APEX-993.pdf) which references the procurement exception. Our tax team is confirming whether reverse-charge applies; I can share certificate / VAT evidence once they confirm early next week.

We prefer to avoid a service freeze as the API endpoints are critical to an ongoing pilot in France. If Redwood needs an express sign-off for a staggered plan, let me know and I will escalate internally.

Best,
Elena Perez
Head of Procurement Operations
Apex Insurance

Attachment: PO-APEX-993.pdf

msg_3_subject: Fwd: Payment freeze proposal & VAT evidence request — Exec credit hold recommendation
msg_3_body:
CONFIDENTIAL — leadership only

Team, forwarding Apex's reply (below). Quick summary and recommended path:

Summary:
- Outstanding: $125,000 (INV-44911), 48 days overdue.
- External proposes 30% by 2028-09-29, remainder by 2028-11-01. PO provided; VAT certificate pending.
- Customer flags active pilot in France — service impact could harm expansion opportunity.

Assessment and ask:
- Revenue at risk if we pull keys: $125k ARR recognition timing + potential churn risk for pilot.
- This is outside standard 30-day terms and exceeds our typical staged-payment tolerance without exec approval.

Recommendation for decision (please reply with yes/no by EOD 2028-09-21):
Option A (recommended): Approve a one-time staggered payment: 30% upfront by 2028-09-29, 70% by 2028-11-01. Place the account on a soft credit hold (no new feature access / rate-limited keys) until first tranche clears. Attach a short mutual action plan (attached) and require VAT evidence before final tranche.

Option B (conservative): Enforce immediate service freeze and escalate to legal for collections.

If approved (Option A), I will draft the amended invoice/payment schedule and route to legal for a short amendment to T&Cs (non-material) and then to finance for the payment staging.

Please see the forwarded message from Elena for details.

— Marissa
SVP, Finance & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
